2d_in_3d_randomness_vis.description: An infoboard displaying 2D randomness algorithms rendered in 3D space, bridging flat visualizations with spatial understanding.
2d_in_3d_randomness_vis.name: 2D in 3D Randomness Visualization
2d_in_3d_randomness_vis.qfep_connection: The flat diagrams of chance — scatter plots, walks, histograms — stood upright in the room. The board bridges the textbook and the terrarium: what the page could only plot, the space around you performs.

GaussianBlurCircle.description: Demonstrates Gaussian blur applied to a circular region, showing how the bell curve kernel creates smooth, natural edge falloff.
GaussianBlurCircle.name: Gaussian Blur Circle
GaussianBlurCircle.qfep_connection: The bell curve applied to sight: a circle dissolving under gaussian blur, each pixel averaged with its neighbors under the curve. The same mathematics that files the draws also softens the world — distribution as a way of seeing.

GaussianBlurShader.description: GPU-accelerated Gaussian blur using a fragment shader. Real-time demonstration of the convolution kernel derived from the normal distribution.
GaussianBlurShader.name: Gaussian Blur Shader

GaussianPaintSplatter.description: Generates paint splatter patterns using Gaussian distribution, creating natural clustering around a center point with density falling off like a bell curve.
GaussianPaintSplatter.name: Gaussian Paint Splatter

MeltingBerniniScene.description: Noise-based vertex displacement applied to classical column geometry. Bernini's baroque forms dissolve under procedural noise fields.
MeltingBerniniScene.name: Melting Bernini Columns
MeltingBerniniScene.qfep_connection: Bernini's columns dissolving under noise-driven vertex displacement: the baroque — history's most deliberate style — surrendered to structured chance. The primitive of the chapter played as elegy: noise does not destroy the form, it *remembers* it while letting it go, coherence draining out neighbor by neighbor.

NoiseColors3D.description: Compares different noise 'colors' (white, pink, brown, blue) in 3D space, visualizing their distinct frequency distributions and correlation properties.
NoiseColors3D.name: Noise Colors 3D
NoiseColors3D.qfep_connection: Noise has colors: white forgets everything, pink remembers a little, brown wanders like a drunk with a heading, blue avoids itself. The gallery of temperaments — proof that 'random' is not one substance but a spectrum of relationships between a sample and its past.

RandomGaussianTexture.description: Generates textures with pixel values sampled from a Gaussian distribution, creating soft, natural-looking noise patterns.
RandomGaussianTexture.name: Random Gaussian Texture

Random_Rotate_Random_XYZ.description: Applies random rotation on all three axes (X, Y, Z), creating fully randomized orientations for chaotic arrangements.
Random_Rotate_Random_XYZ.name: Random Rotate XYZ
Random_Rotate_Random_XYZ.qfep_connection: The room's namesake engine: grid cubes spun by three independent draws, one per axis. Orientation surrendered to chance while position holds — the grid keeping order in one register and losing it in another, which is the whole trick of controlled entropy.

RotateGridCubes.description: Gradient slope test with animated rotation for walkability check.
RotateGridCubes.name: Slope Gradient Cubes

VoxelNoiseROIs.description: Voxel noise with regions of interest (ROIs) — isolated volumes where different noise parameters or thresholds apply, useful for terrain biomes.
VoxelNoiseROIs.name: Voxel Noise ROIs

WhiteNoiseGallery.description: A gallery showcasing pure white noise — uniform random values with no correlation between samples. The baseline for understanding structured noise types.
WhiteNoiseGallery.name: White Noise Gallery
WhiteNoiseGallery.qfep_connection: The baseline: pure white noise, every sample a stranger to its neighbors. This is randomness before it learns to remember — the hiss the whole chapter is a departure from. Hang it first so every other room can be measured as distance from amnesia.

bell_alley.description: Constructs a corridor of cubes along Z that widens according to a Gaussian bell curve, creating a passage that narrows at the center and expands at the edges.
bell_alley.name: Bell Curve Alley

blue_noise.description: Interactive blue noise generation for high-quality random sampling and distribution
blue_noise.name: Blue Noise

bubble_particles.description: Movement-based procedural bubble system — bubbles spawn in a configurable area, rise with randomized speeds and sizes, fade over time, and pop with synthesized audio. Concurrent sound limiting and pitch variation create an organic underwater soundscape.
bubble_particles.name: Bubble Particles

bubbles_random.description: A particle system that generates random bubble effects with dynamic spawning
bubbles_random.name: Random Bubbles

cloudvolume.description: 3D volumetric cloud generation using noise algorithms for atmospheric and sky effects
cloudvolume.name: Cloud Volume

coin_toss.description: The simplest random experiment. Grab coins from a tray and toss them. A counter tracks the heads/tails ratio converging to 0.5 over many flips. Gold side = heads, silver side = tails.
coin_toss.name: Coin Toss
coin_toss.qfep_connection: Bernoulli trial — the atom of probability. p = 0.5 as perfect symmetry.

crystal_random_walk_demo.description: Random walk constrained to a crystal lattice structure, demonstrating how geometric constraints shape stochastic paths into crystalline forms.
crystal_random_walk_demo.name: Crystal Random Walk Demo

curl_noise_particles.description: Divergence-free curl noise driving 300 particles in smooth swirling ribbons. Cross product of two noise gradients guarantees incompressible flow. Particles color-shift from deep blue (slow) through cyan to white (fast), with trailing flow lines for visualization.
curl_noise_particles.name: Curl Noise Particles

dice_throw.description: A VR dice on a felt table. Grab and throw the dice — roll a 6 and 100 balls rain from the sky, roll a 1 and just 1 ball falls. Tracks roll statistics showing convergence to discrete uniform distribution with expected value 3.5.
dice_throw.name: Dice Throw
dice_throw.qfep_connection: Equiprobability — each face equally likely. Fairness as geometric symmetry.

digital_materiality_glitch.description: Interactive exploration of digital materiality through glitch aesthetics and algorithmic artifacts
digital_materiality_glitch.name: Digital Materiality Glitch
digital_materiality_glitch.qfep_connection: The glitch as digital matter showing its grain: corruption arranged as revelation. When bits misfire the smooth surface confesses it was always discrete underneath — randomness used as a solvent for the illusion of continuity.

distribution_visualization.description: Interactive visualization of statistical distributions and probability patterns
distribution_visualization.name: Distribution Visualization

entropy_axiom.description: Visualizes the gradient from order to chaos using a 10x10x40 MultiMesh grid (4000 instances). Points transition from structured alignment to random displacement along the Z-axis.
entropy_axiom.name: Entropy Axiom

entropy_jar.description: A glass jar of red and blue particles on a pedestal. Grab and shake to mix them — they never unmix. Live Shannon entropy readout tracks disorder. The second law of thermodynamics felt physically through VR interaction.
entropy_jar.name: Entropy Jar
entropy_jar.qfep_connection: Irreversibility — mixing is easy, unmixing is impossible. The arrow of time made tangible through embodied interaction.

env_one.description: A procedural environment generation algorithm using randomness for kitbashing
env_one.name: Environment One
env_one.qfep_connection: A whole environment kitbashed by draw: parts picked, placed, and joined by chance. The room-scale claim of the chapter — not an object randomized, but a *place* that entropy furnished.

evolutionary_algorithms.description: Particle system demonstrating selection, mutation, and crossover. Populations evolve toward fitness goals through randomized genetic operations.
evolutionary_algorithms.name: Evolutionary Algorithms
evolutionary_algorithms.qfep_connection: Selection, mutation, crossover running live: populations drifting toward fitness. Among the fractals it plays the wild cousin — recursion through generations instead of through geometry, the rule rewriting its own parameters as it goes.

extreme_randomness.description: Interactive particle-based extreme randomness generation and visualization
extreme_randomness.name: Extreme Randomness
extreme_randomness.qfep_connection: Randomness at full amplitude: particles driven by draws with no damping, no distribution's comfort. The room's outer limit — past structure, past statistics-as-shape — where entropy stops being a resource and becomes weather.

galton_board.description: Balls drop through a triangular peg array. Each peg deflects left or right with equal probability. After many rows, the bin counts form a binomial distribution converging to a Gaussian bell curve. VR buttons: DROP, AUTO, RESET, SPEED.
galton_board.name: Galton Board
galton_board.qfep_connection: CLT as convergence — many independent binary choices accumulate into Gaussian structure. Order from repetition.

gaussian_random.description: A bell curve algorithm that creates natural-looking height distributions
gaussian_random.name: Gaussian Generator
gaussian_random.qfep_connection: The gaussian source itself — draws clustered around a mean, rare at the tails. Uniform chance says anywhere; gaussian chance says near here, mostly. The difference between noise and temperament.

hardware_entropy_decay.description: Your VR movements become entropy. Controller velocity drives scratches, grip pressure accumulates grime, head rotation feeds weathering rate. Three display surfaces (cube, sphere, cylinder) decay in real-time from your hardware inputs via a custom procedural shader.
hardware_entropy_decay.name: Hardware Entropy Decay
hardware_entropy_decay.qfep_connection: Entropy from embodiment — the observer's physical presence is the source of randomness that degrades order.

height_random.description: An elevation algorithm that randomly raises cubes to create landscapes
height_random.name: Height Distributor
height_random.qfep_connection: Chance is granted an 8x8 region, 150 raises, and a hard ceiling, then looped back to zero. Randomness reads as landscape only inside the fence the grid concedes to it — and the fence resets.

instancingscatter.description: High-performance instance scattering algorithm for procedural object placement and distribution
instancingscatter.name: Instancing Scatter
instancingscatter.qfep_connection: Five thousand objects, three MultiMeshes: abundance as a compression trick, every crystal a transform on a shared body. The meadow is dense precisely because nothing in it is individual.

marchingcubes_voxel_noise_demo.description: Marching cubes algorithm applied to a 3D noise field. Generates smooth isosurface mesh from voxel density values.
marchingcubes_voxel_noise_demo.name: Marching Cubes Voxel Noise

monte_carlo_dartboard.description: Throw darts at a square with an inscribed circle. The ratio of inside/outside hits converges to pi/4. Live counter shows estimate of pi improving with each dart. Green dots inside circle, red dots outside.
monte_carlo_dartboard.name: Monte Carlo Dart Board
monte_carlo_dartboard.qfep_connection: Computation through accumulation — random sampling converges to mathematical truth.

neon_wave_grid.description: Interactive Perlin noise-based neon wave grid with dynamic lighting effects
neon_wave_grid.name: Neon Wave Grid

noise_mixer.description: Fractal Brownian Motion noise mixer — layers multiple sin-based noise octaves with controllable lacunarity and persistence. 128x128 floor texture with earth-tone color ramp. VR sliders adjust octaves (1–8), lacunarity (1.5–3.0), and persistence (0.3–0.7) to explore how complexity emerges from layered simple functions.
noise_mixer.name: Noise Mixer

noise_space.description: Interactive 3D noise exploration space. Walk through a procedurally generated environment driven by configurable noise parameters.
noise_space.name: Noise Space Explorer
noise_space.qfep_connection: The chapter's thesis as a place: a whole environment driven by configurable noise, walked from inside. Not an exhibit about noise — an exhibit *made of* it, where changing a parameter re-decides the room around you.

noise_terrain.description: Interactive procedural terrain generation using various noise algorithms and height mapping
noise_terrain.name: Noise Terrain
noise_terrain.qfep_connection: Noise cashed out as landscape: height mapped from the field, terrain without a designer. The first honest answer to 'where do procedural worlds come from' — from correlation, tuned.

noise_terrain_with_blobs.description: Advanced noise terrain generator with animated blob particles that move across the landscape using spatial shaders and dynamic positioning
noise_terrain_with_blobs.name: Noise Terrain with Animated Blobs

noiselayers.description: Demonstrates octave layering (fractal Brownian motion) by stacking multiple noise frequencies. Shows how combining scales creates natural complexity.
noiselayers.name: Noise Layers

noisesphere.description: Noise-deformed hemisphere rendered with the planet shader for atmospheric dome effects.
noisesphere.name: noisesphere
noisesphere.qfep_connection: A hemisphere deformed by noise and dressed in the planet shader: a world's skin grown from correlation. The dome overhead is the chapter's quiet claim to scale — planets are noise seen from far enough away.

noisetext.description: Applies the noise planet shader to 3D text and a plinth for animated logo signage.
noisetext.name: noisetext

noisetorus.description: Shader-driven torus whose surface ripples with animated noise and hue shifting.
noisetorus.name: noisetorus
noisetorus.qfep_connection: Kept in permanent mild weather: animated noise displaces the torus's vertices while the hue drifts, and TIME is wrapped at 3600 seconds so the flux never accumulates. Endless change engineered to loop — E_flux on a one-hour lease.

omoss.description: Interactive Omoss algorithm for procedural organic growth and pattern generation
omoss.name: Omoss

perlin_noise.description: Interactive Perlin noise generation and visualization
perlin_noise.name: Perlin Noise
perlin_noise.qfep_connection: Perlin's gift to graphics: gradients on a lattice, interpolated smoothly — randomness that flows instead of stutters. Every organic-looking surface in games descends from this trick. The demo hands you the dials: octaves stacking detail, persistence deciding how loudly the small scales speak.

perlin_noise_clouds.description: Interactive 3D volumetric cloud generation using Perlin noise for atmospheric and procedural sky effects
perlin_noise_clouds.name: Perlin Noise Clouds

perlin_noise_terrain.description: Interactive 3D terrain generation using Perlin noise algorithms
perlin_noise_terrain.name: Perlin Noise Terrain
perlin_noise_terrain.qfep_connection: The Perlin pipeline run to its natural end: octaves become mountain ranges, persistence becomes ruggedness. Parameter names turn geological — the chapter's clearest case of mathematics wearing the world's clothes.

perlinvolume.description: 3D Perlin noise volume generation for procedural content creation and spatial algorithms
perlinvolume.name: Perlin Volume
perlinvolume.qfep_connection: All the work happens in the shader's ray march; the script only spins the box. Noise here is not scattered points but a solid you can look into — coherence as a volume, resampled by every ray.

pheromone_terrain.description: Swarm-based terrain generation where agents deposit pheromone trails that shape the landscape. Demonstrates emergent self-organization from simple local rules.
pheromone_terrain.name: Pheromone Terrain

pickup_cube_placer.description: Finds the active grid system and populates pickup cubes using randomized or patterned placement modes.
pickup_cube_placer.name: pickup_cube_placer

pipe_dream.description: A 3D recreation of the classic Windows Pipes screensaver. Grows a colored pipe that randomly changes direction, building an intricate network over 100 segments.
pipe_dream.name: Pipe Dream
pipe_dream.qfep_connection: The Windows Pipes screensaver reborn: a pipe growing by random turns, filling the volume with plumbing nobody designed. Idle-machine art — the desktop's oldest proof that a few dice and a growth rule can furnish a world.

pixel_cloud.description: Builds an upward-biased self-avoiding random walk and places cubes along the path to form a pixel cloud sculpture.
pixel_cloud.name: pixel_cloud

plane_manipulator.description: This script animates a random walk on a 3D plane. It simulates walkers that move across the plane's surface, raising the ground to create trails in real-time.
plane_manipulator.name: plane_manipulator
plane_manipulator.qfep_connection: The walk is not drawn on the surface; it becomes the surface. Each walker raises the ground it crosses into a trail, and the untouched border is the only place the plane remembers being flat.

plane_random.description: Generates a planar surface with random vertex displacement, creating organic undulating terrain from flat geometry.
plane_random.name: Plane Random
plane_random.qfep_connection: One vertex per second, plus or minus half a meter, forever: terrain here is not designed but accrued, and the heightmap collider keeps pace so your feet ratify each coin flip as ground.

pollock_3d.description: Interactive 3D Jackson Pollock-inspired art using movement-based procedural randomness
pollock_3d.name: Pollock 3D

pollock_painting_in_3d.description: Interactive 3D Jackson Pollock-inspired painting using movement-based procedural randomness
pollock_painting_in_3d.name: Pollock Painting in 3D

pool_hole_noise.description: Interactive cellular noise generation with pool hole pattern visualization
pool_hole_noise.name: Pool Hole Noise

prng_crank_machine.description: A physical pseudo-random number generator machine. Press CRANK to step the LCG formula: state = (state * 1664525 + 1013904223) mod 2^32. Each step animates multiply, add, mod phases. Shows deterministic sequence, normalized 0-1 output, and full history.
prng_crank_machine.name: PRNG Crank Machine
prng_crank_machine.qfep_connection: Determinism masquerading as randomness — structure hidden in apparent chaos.

probability_distributions_3d.description: Interactive 3D visualization of various probability distributions and statistical patterns
probability_distributions_3d.name: Probability Distributions 3D

random_bell_curve.description: Builds a 20x20 quad grid shaped into a 3D Gaussian bell curve with HeightMapShape3D collisions. Optional surface noise adds organic variation.
random_bell_curve.name: Random Bell Curve Terrain
random_bell_curve.qfep_connection: The bell made object: samples piling into the curve that chance keeps its accounts in. No single draw knows about the bell; the bell knows about all of them.

random_butterflies.description: Entropy-seeking butterfly swarm: wander randomly then land on entropy_axiom grid points, wings tinting blue-to-red along the order-chaos gradient. Grab and release to send to a new entropy point.
random_butterflies.name: Random Butterflies
random_butterflies.qfep_connection: Butterflies scattered by draw — position, wing-beat, drift all sampled. The prettiest argument in the room that entropy is freedom: nothing places them, and that is why they look alive.

random_color_book_page_collection.description: Interactive collection of randomly generated colored book pages using procedural algorithms
random_color_book_page_collection.name: Random Color Book Page Collection
random_color_book_page_collection.qfep_connection: The RAND million-random-digits book re-typeset in color: indexed rows, a side number scaled from the 1955 original, every swatch a fresh randf() — staging the bureaucratic labor it once took to publish disorder as a reference work.

random_decay_multimesh.description: Two standing 2D decay stacks rendered with MultiMesh: 1m cubes and 1dm prisms that gradually drift, rotate, sink, and darken.
random_decay_multimesh.name: Random Decay MultiMesh

random_decay_objects.description: Interactive visualization of random decay processes and object degradation
random_decay_objects.name: Random Decay Objects

random_edge_profile.description: A planar surface that generates random edge profiles and patterns
random_edge_profile.name: Random Edge Profile
random_edge_profile.qfep_connection: Chance under clamped boundary conditions: the heights are pure RNG draws, but the profile is forced to start and end at 0.5. Randomness admitted only in the interior; the frame stays negotiated.

random_edge_profile_collection.description: Interactive collection of random edge profiles for procedural geometry generation
random_edge_profile_collection.name: Random Edge Profile Collection

random_gaussian_texture.description: Interactive Gaussian distribution texture generation for natural random patterns
random_gaussian_texture.name: Random Gaussian Texture

random_number_book_page_1955.description: A single page from the RAND Corporation 1955 random digit table. Numbers cascade live top-to-bottom. Touch any 5-digit number to freeze it in amber — the rest keep flowing.
random_number_book_page_1955.name: Random Number Book Page 1955
random_number_book_page_1955.qfep_connection: A page from A Million Random Digits (RAND, 1955) — the book nobody reads and everybody trusted. Before hardware entropy, randomness was a print run: tables harvested from an electronic roulette, proofread for bias, sold to scientists who needed disorder they could cite. Chance with an ISBN — the moment entropy became infrastructure.

random_number_book_page_collection.description: RAND Corporation 1955 random digit table brought to life. Numbers cascade top-to-bottom like a stock ticker. Touch any number in VR to freeze it — frozen numbers glow amber while the rest keep flowing. Demonstrates that randomness is a process, not a snapshot.
random_number_book_page_collection.name: Random Number Book — Live Cascade
random_number_book_page_collection.qfep_connection: Randomness as flow — freezing a number is an act of observation that collapses possibility into fixed value.

random_plants.description: Interactive procedural plant generation with random growth patterns and organic forms
random_plants.name: Random Plants
random_plants.qfep_connection: A hundred draws against four probability sliders sort the world into tree, bush, flower, grass: variety as budget allocation, the taxonomy fixed before the first trunk is placed.

random_transformations.description: Interactive visualization of random geometric transformations and spatial manipulations
random_transformations.name: Random Transformations

random_transformations_geometric.name: Random Transformations - Geometric
random_transformations_geometric.qfep_connection: Geometry under dice: translate, rotate, scale, each parameter drawn. The form survives as a family resemblance across its own variations — identity loosened, not lost. Entropy applied to shape is variation; applied without bound, dissolution.

random_walk_128.description: Fine-grained random walk on 128x128 grid using tiny cubes
random_walk_128.name: Random Walk 128x128
random_walk_128.qfep_connection: A walk at 128x128 grain: one wanderer, tiny steps, no memory. The fine grid turns the walk's statistics visible — dense scribble near the origin, thinning frontier — chance accumulating into a shape no single step intended.

random_walk_collection.description: Interactive paper that demonstrates random walk algorithms with grab and manipulation capabilities
random_walk_collection.name: Random Walk Grab Paper
random_walk_collection.qfep_connection: Many walks released together: each path senseless alone, the ensemble growing the square-root halo the mathematics promised. The collection is the lesson — randomness has laws, but only in the plural.

random_walk_grab_paper.description: Interactive paper that demonstrates random walk algorithms with grab and manipulation capabilities
random_walk_grab_paper.name: Random Walk Grab Paper

random_walk_leash.description: A glowing orb on a leash that tugs in random directions. Grab it in VR and feel the random walk through your hand. The orb pulses with each impulse. A trail traces the walk path. Stats track drift vs sqrt(N) theoretical scaling.
random_walk_leash.name: Random Walk Leash
random_walk_leash.qfep_connection: Embodied randomness — the walk isn't watched, it's felt. Your arm becomes the accumulator of stochastic impulses.

randomize_cubes_over_Z.description: Distributes cubes with increasing randomness along the Z-axis, visualizing a gradient from order to disorder.
randomize_cubes_over_Z.name: Randomize Cubes Over Z

randomlines.description: ImmediateMesh random line segments with 3 distributions (uniform/Gaussian/clustered), 3 color modes (solid/golden-ratio/length-gradient), optional drift animation and bounding box. Config: num_lines, area_size_x/y/z, distribution, cluster_count, cluster_spread, color_mode, animate, drift_speed, show_bounding_box
randomlines.name: Random Lines

randompoint.description: Drops a single draggable point inside an XY bounds and keeps its billboarded coordinate label in range.
randompoint.name: randompoint

randompoints.capacity: DISTINGUISH structured randomness from uniform randomness by seeing how a single constraint (minimum distance) transforms a point cloud from chaos to jazz
randompoints.description: Three distributions reveal three relationships with space. Uniform scatters without memory — each point ignores every other. Gaussian clusters around a center — proximity is destiny. Blue noise enforces minimum distance via dart-throwing rejection, structured randomness where emptiness is forbidden. The critical parameter is blue_noise_min_dist: the exclusion radius that converts white noise into jazz. Contrasts with randompoint (single white noise); prepares for Perlin noise (structured randomness with continuity).
interactions: observe packing limit in blue noise mode
randompoints.name: randompoints

parameters.blue_noise_min_dist: Minimum distance for blue noise rejection (default: 0.25)

randompoints.qfep_connection: Pure E(S) — three distributions at three lambda values. Uniform is maximum entropy (lambda=0). Gaussian introduces spatial bias (lambda rising). Blue noise enforces a minimum-distance constraint that converts raw entropy into structured randomness — lambda at full strength, where constraint produces beauty, not order.

randompoints_gaussian.description: Variant of the grab-point scatter preconfigured to sample from a 3D Gaussian cloud with labeled spheres.
randompoints_gaussian.name: randompoints_gaussian

randompoints_uniform.description: Scatters grab spheres uniformly through a bounding box and labels each point.
randompoints_uniform.name: randompoints_uniform

randomup.description: Randomly elevates objects upward with varying heights, demonstrating basic vertical displacement using uniform randomness.
randomup.name: Random Up
randomup.qfep_connection: A coin weighted 60-40 toward heaven builds the palace: each upward win lays a three-metre slope cube so the climb stays walkable, and a nav graph records every wager. Architecture as accumulated bias — the building is the histogram of its own coin flips.

rejection_sampling_demo.description: Visual scatter plot of the accept/reject method for sampling arbitrary distributions. 2000 uniform random points plotted against a Gaussian target curve — green dots accepted (below curve), red dots rejected (above). Shows acceptance ratio.
rejection_sampling_demo.name: Rejection Sampling Demo

remove_random.description: A demolition algorithm that randomly removes cubes from the grid
remove_random.name: Random Destructor
remove_random.qfep_connection: The demolition primitive: cubes deleted by chance, the grid thinned by dice. Where every other builder in this world adds, this one subtracts without a plan — and the room that remains is a negative sculpture of the sequence of draws. Entropy as an editor.

rotate_grid_cubes.description: A grid of cubes rotated in repeating row-based patterns. The lattice stays fixed while orientation changes propagate across it, making the difference between flat and tilted sections immediately readable. Animation exposes rotation as a patterned field rather than a single isolated action. It shows how a transformation can be distributed across a structure.
rotate_grid_cubes.name: Rotate Grid Cubes
rotate_grid_cubes.qfep_connection: Transformation modifies orientation across S while the grid itself remains stable. Patterned rotation makes state change legible as repetition and variation on a fixed lattice.
rotate_grid_cubes.capacity: READ patterned rotation across a fixed lattice and compare flat rows against tilted ones.
interactions: watch the rotation pattern move across rows
change rot_amount and rot_amount_y to reshape the pattern
compare flat sections with rotated ramps or slopes

rotate_random_y.description: Applies random Y-axis rotation to objects, creating varied orientations while maintaining vertical alignment.
rotate_random_y.name: Rotate Random Y
rotate_random_y.qfep_connection: One pass at load: every instanced cube nudged around Y by a random fraction of a degree, then left alone forever. The imperceptible wobble is what keeps the MultiMesh from confessing itself — sameness needs a pinch of noise to read as world rather than copy.

sculpt_one.description: An artistic sculpting algorithm that randomly modifies and shapes geometric forms
sculpt_one.name: Sculpt One
sculpt_one.qfep_connection: Sculpting by random modification: a form shaped by accepting the dice's suggestions. The sculptor keeps only the veto — chance proposes every stroke. Authorship as curation of accidents.

shader_07_noise.description: Book of Shaders chapter 7 — value noise, gradient noise, simplex noise implemented as GPU shaders on a quad display.
shader_07_noise.name: Shader Noise Functions

shader_08_cellularnoise.description: Book of Shaders chapter 8 — Voronoi and Worley noise patterns rendered as GPU shaders. Shows distance fields and cell boundaries.
shader_08_cellularnoise.name: Cellular Noise Shader

shader_noise_space.description: Interactive shader-based noise space exploration with procedural textures and patterns
shader_noise_space.name: Shader Noise Space
shader_noise_space.qfep_connection: Noise evaluated per-pixel at framerate: the GPU as noise organ, procedural texture with no texture stored. The room turns as you move because nothing in it is a picture — everything is a function, sampled where you look.

shannon_entropy_meter.description: Wall-mounted Shannon entropy gauge — generates a random sequence, computes symbol frequencies, and displays H = -Σ p(x) log₂ p(x). Bar gauge fills from 0 to max entropy (~3.32 bits for 10 symbols). Frequency histogram shows symbol distribution.
shannon_entropy_meter.name: Shannon Entropy Meter

simplex_noise.description: Interactive Simplex noise generation and visualization for high-quality procedural content
simplex_noise.name: Simplex Noise
simplex_noise.qfep_connection: Perlin's own second draft: the simplex grid replaces squares, fewer artifacts, better behavior in high dimensions. Standing beside its ancestor it teaches versioning as a mathematical practice — even noise gets revised.

slot_machine.description: A classic slot machine with 3 spinning reels. Pull the VR lever to spin — reels stop one by one, left to right. Tracks a histogram of symbol frequencies showing convergence to uniform distribution. Triple matches flash gold. AUTO mode for rapid sampling.
slot_machine.name: Slot Machine
slot_machine.qfep_connection: Independence — each reel is an independent uniform trial. The combination space grows multiplicatively (6^3 = 216 outcomes).

spawn_randomcubes.description: Interactive 3D Jackson Pollock-inspired painting using movement-based procedural randomness
spawn_randomcubes.name: spawn_randomcubes

ten_print.description: Interactive recreation of the classic Commodore 64 10 PRINT maze generation algorithm
ten_print.name: 10 PRINT

ten_print_maze_3d.description: Extrudes the classic 10 PRINT pattern into a standing maze and animates an ant pathfinder through it.
ten_print_maze_3d.name: ten_print_maze_3d
ten_print_maze_3d.qfep_connection: The 10 PRINT coin flip stood up into walls that keep re-rolling on a timer, while an ant recomputes its route through them: one bit per cell is enough to turn navigation into a live negotiation instead of a solved map.

tessellation_lattice_demo.description: Random walk on tessellated lattice structures (triangular, hexagonal, square), showing how tiling geometry affects diffusion patterns.
tessellation_lattice_demo.name: Tessellation Lattice Demo
tessellation_lattice_demo.qfep_connection: The tessellation exists whole before the first cell appears: a shuffled walk path merely grants visibility, one space-filling polyhedron at a time, then loops and forgets. Discovery staged over a fully determined lattice — chance decides only the order of appearance, never what there is.

trng_vs_prng.description: Interactive comparison between True Random Number Generators and Pseudo-Random Number Generators
trng_vs_prng.name: TRNG vs PRNG
trng_vs_prng.qfep_connection: The chapter's founding trial: the crank versus the harvest. A PRNG is determinism wearing a costume — same seed, same sequence, forever replayable. A TRNG listens to the world (decay, thermal hiss) and cannot repeat itself even if asked. Standing between them you learn that most computed randomness is a performance of freedom, and real entropy has to be gathered, not made.

value_noise.description: Interactive Value noise generation and visualization for procedural texture creation
value_noise.name: Value Noise

voxelnoise.description: 3D noise visualized as voxels — cubes appear or disappear based on noise threshold, revealing the underlying scalar field as solid geometry.
voxelnoise.name: Voxel Noise
voxelnoise.qfep_connection: 3D noise made walkable census: cubes appear where the field crosses threshold, vanish where it does not. The invisible correlation structure of the noise stands revealed as architecture — you are looking at the field's memory, cell by cell.

walk_random.description: An algorithmic walker that creates trails through the grid space
walk_random.name: Random Walker

walkingsphere.description: Spike, Random walk, Cellular automata  sphere
walkingsphere.name: walkingsphere

worley_noise.description: Voronoi/cellular noise texture on a floor quad. Scatters random seed points and computes F2-F1 (second-nearest minus nearest distance) for the classic cell boundary look. Complement to Perlin/Simplex noise.
worley_noise.name: Worley Noise

seed_replay_demo.name: Seed Replay Demo
seed_replay_demo.description: Demonstrates seed reproducibility — an 8x8 grid of colored cubes generated from a seed. Same seed always produces the same pattern. Slider changes seed, Replay regenerates identically, Random picks a new seed.

distribution_comparator.name: Distribution Comparator
distribution_comparator.description: Side-by-side comparison of 3 probability distributions — Uniform (blue), Gaussian (green), Exponential (orange). Three columns of 16 histogram bars generated from the same sample count. Slider scales samples from 100 to 10000; resample button regenerates all three.
distribution_comparator.qfep_connection: Three distributions from one random source — the channeling rule (F) determines shape. Uniform is maximum entropy; Gaussian is the attractor of summation; Exponential is memoryless decay. Same randomness, different constraints, different forms.

perlin_noise_bridge.description: Side-by-side 16x16 heightfield grids comparing white noise (chaotic) and Perlin noise (terrain-like). Shows how gradient noise transforms raw randomness into coherent structure through spatial memory.
perlin_noise_bridge.name: Perlin Noise Bridge

reaction_diffusion_intro.description: A 32x32 Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion simulation rendered as an ImageTexture. Two chemicals U and V interact to produce spots, stripes, or coral patterns from random initial conditions — Turing morphogenesis made visible.
reaction_diffusion_intro.name: Reaction-Diffusion Intro

rejection_toy.name: Rejection Toy (held - under the curve)
rejection_toy.description: Hand-scale rejection sampling: dots scattered in a box, the ones under the target curve kept (green), the rest refused. Sample any shape by throwing away what does not fit.

rejection_bench.name: Rejection Bench (accept / reject)
rejection_bench.description: Bench rejection sampling: darts fill a panel under a target curve, accepted ones build a histogram of the shape beside it.

rejection_room.name: Rejection Room (walk-in accept / reject)
rejection_room.description: Room-scale rejection sampling: a giant target curve, darts raining through the volume, accepted ones glowing into the distribution on the floor.

pi_dart_toy.name: Pi Dart Toy (held Monte Carlo)
pi_dart_toy.description: Hand-scale Monte Carlo: darts speckle a square with an inscribed quarter-circle; the inside/total ratio estimates pi. Estimate the unknowable by throwing enough darts.

pi_dart_bench.name: Pi Dart Bench (pi convergence)
pi_dart_bench.description: Bench Monte Carlo: hundreds of darts accumulate and a convergence line tightens the running pi estimate toward 3.14159.

pi_dart_room.name: Pi Dart Room (stand in the square)
pi_dart_room.description: Room-scale Monte Carlo: you stand in the unit square as darts rain - inside the circle green, outside red - and the floor ratio reads pi.

coin_dice_bench.name: Coin & Dice Bench (discrete tallies)
coin_dice_bench.description: Bench of discrete chance: a flipping coin and a tumbling die feed two live bar charts that trend toward uniform.

dice_rain_room.name: Dice Rain Room (raining histogram)
dice_rain_room.description: Room-scale discrete chance: dice rain from the ceiling and settle into six columns by face, building a roughly flat (uniform) histogram.

random_walk_bench.name: Random Walk Bench (drunkard path)
random_walk_bench.description: Bench random walk: a token steps at random across a tabletop grid, trailing the path it has wandered - each step a fresh coin.

distribution_bench.name: Distribution Bench (live histogram)
distribution_bench.description: Bench distribution: beads fall into bins and a twelve-bar histogram holds its shape - not all outcomes are equal.

perlin_bench.name: Perlin Bench (coherent curve)
perlin_bench.description: Bench Perlin noise: a smooth, coherent 1D curve flows across a panel with a marker riding it - noise with neighbours.

noise_compare_bench.name: Noise Compare Bench (value / simplex / worley)
noise_compare_bench.description: Bench comparison of three coherent noises side by side - value, simplex, and worley - so their textures read against each other.

noise_displacer.name: Noise Displacer (surface displacement)
noise_displacer.description: A tool: a simplex field displacing a flat surface into rolling hills in real time. Coherent noise doing the job of shaping geometry.

noise_flow_drones.name: Noise Flow Drones (flow-field navigation)
noise_flow_drones.description: A swarm steered by a Perlin flow field - the noise field doing the real job of navigation, each drone reading the value at its feet.

noise_height_toy.name: Noise Height Toy (held heightfield)
noise_height_toy.description: The smallest 'noise = height': a little tile of cells whose heights come from a noise field, undulating in the hand.

noise_dunes_bench.name: Noise Dunes Bench (tabletop landscape)
noise_dunes_bench.description: Bench landscape: a noise field read as height becomes drifting dunes, low sand to pale ridge.

noise_terrain_forge.name: Noise Terrain Forge (stamps ground)
noise_terrain_forge.description: A tool: a forge that stamps a walkable noise-terrain patch - turning a noise field into usable ground.

blue_noise_toy.name: Blue Noise Toy (even-spaced points)
blue_noise_toy.description: Hand-scale blue noise: points placed by best-candidate so each keeps its distance - random without clumping.

blue_noise_bench.name: Blue Noise Bench (white vs blue)
blue_noise_bench.description: Bench comparison: the same count of points placed as white noise (clumpy) and blue noise (even) side by side.

blue_noise_planter.name: Blue Noise Planter (even placement)
blue_noise_planter.description: A tool: scattering props with blue-noise spacing so they never clump - even placement doing a real job.

seed_toy.name: Seed Toy (same seed, same glyph)
seed_toy.description: Hand-scale determinism: a seed dial grows a glyph; the same seed always grows the same one - pseudo-randomness in disguise.

seed_bench.name: Seed Bench (same seed, same stream)
seed_bench.description: Bench determinism: two generators fed the same seed produce identical streams; flip one bit and they diverge forever.

entropy_bench.name: Entropy Bench (bits of surprise)
entropy_bench.description: Bench entropy: a biasable source whose Shannon entropy reads from one bit at fair down toward zero as the bias grows.

markov_melody.name: Markov Melody (chain composes)
markov_melody.description: A tool: a Markov chain hopping a ring of note-states to compose a melody - the memoryless chain doing real work.

jitter_bench.name: Jitter Bench (perturb the grid)
jitter_bench.description: Bench of random transforms: a tidy grid of cubes dissolved from order into noise as the jitter dial rises.

ten_print_toy.name: Ten Print Toy (maze of slashes)
ten_print_toy.description: Hand-scale 10 PRINT: one coin-flip per cell draws a slash or backslash, and a maze appears - the smallest generative grammar.

ten_print_bench.name: Ten Print Bench (bias dial)
ten_print_bench.description: Bench 10 PRINT: a larger maze panel whose character shifts as a slash/backslash probability dial biases the coin.

ten_print_textile.name: Ten Print Textile (fabric loom)
ten_print_textile.description: A tool: 10 PRINT as a textile loom, weaving an endless bolt of slash/backslash fabric - the pattern doing a design job.

scatter_bench.name: Scatter Bench (Pollock drips)
scatter_bench.description: Bench of generative art: chance as a brush, flinging drips and splatters across a canvas at bench scale.

random_fireworks.name: Random Fireworks (per-particle chance)
random_fireworks.description: A tool: fireworks whose particles each get their own random velocity and colour - individual chance making an emergent display.

lottery_drum.name: Lottery Drum (uniform raffle)
lottery_drum.description: A tool: a tumbling raffle drum ejecting one numbered ball, each equally likely - uniform RNG doing a real picking job.

dna_sprout.name: DNA Sprout (held seed -> plant)
dna_sprout.description: The held end of seed -> form: a deterministic CritterDNA genome grown by an L-system into one plant. Same seed always grows the same plant - the deep seed, not flat randomness. Bridges seed_toy to the DNA galleries.

genome_bench.name: Genome Bench (scrub -> regrow)
genome_bench.description: Bench genotype-to-phenotype: a CritterDNA genome drifts by small mutations and the plant re-grows each change. The row of gene-bars is the seed - store the numbers and the form returns.

seed_vs_random.name: Seed vs Random (the thesis bed)
seed_vs_random.description: The payoff: two beds. LEFT grows from fresh randomness every few seconds - never the same, nothing to store. RIGHT grows from fixed CritterDNA seeds - store the seed, regrow it exactly. Flat randomness vs the deep, side by side.

galton_friction.description: Two solutions to the Galton bell side by side — THE HARVEST (real physics, a falling body, lumpy and never repeating) vs THE CRANK (pseudo, bin = sum(randf() < 0.5), instant and perfect and reproducible). The crank is smaller because it is cheaper: real randomness is too expensive or too specific to keep everywhere.
galton_friction.name: Galton Friction
galton_friction.qfep_connection: The manufactured vs the harvested — real randomness is expensive and specific; what the system holds is the crank. The bell you trust is almost always made.
